context: A woman phones a music school to book a trial piano lesson for her son.

lines.text: This is the IELTS Listening Test, Practice Test Five. There are four sections. Write all your answers on the answer sheet as you listen. You will hear each recording once only.
Now turn to Section One. You will hear a woman phoning a music school to book a trial lesson.
Questions one to five. Complete the form below. Write no more than three words and/or a number for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions one to five.
Look at the example.
Good morning, Westbridge Music School, Greg speaking.
Hello — I'd like to book a trial lesson, please.
lines.note: Worked EXAMPLE: Reason for call — Trial lesson. Not scored.

lines.text: Now listen and answer questions one to five.
Of course. Can I take your first name?
It's Yasmin.
lines.note: First name printed on the paper as Yasmin — not scored.

lines.text: Thanks, Yasmin. And your surname?
Venkatesh — that's V, E, N, K, A, T, E, S, H.
Got that. A contact number, please?
Oh-seven-nine-two-two, four-one-eight, zero-six-three.
And the instrument — guitar is what most beginners start on.
Not guitar — piano. He already has a keyboard at home.
I can offer you the ninth of May at five o'clock.
The ninth is a school concert — is the eighth free?
Yes — the eighth of May, same week. I had the concert date open by mistake.
Five is a bit late — could we do quarter to five?
Quarter to five — that's sixteen forty-five. I'll put that down.
Questions six to ten. Complete the form below. Write no more than three words and/or a number for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions six to ten.
Now listen and answer questions six to ten.
A few details about the student. What's his name?
Rafi.
And how old is he?
Nine — nine years old.
Would you like a theory booklet as well as the lesson?
Yes — add the theory booklet, please.
I'll add theory booklet to the notes.
Parking is on Mill Street behind the hall — Mill Street.
Your booking code is W-B, dash, four-four-one-nine.
That's great, thank you.
See you on the eighth. Bye for now.
That is the end of Section One. Now turn to Section Two.
